claim: ARH disproves the Platonic Representation Hypothesis, so PRH-motivated methods (like OPRD-Bridge PCA+MSE) rest on a falsified premise.

votes.reasoning:
ARH's own authors and independent secondary sources (arxiviq, EPFL project page, techxplore) converge: the paper is titled "Revisiting," not "Refuting," and explicitly frames itself as refinement — global spectral metrics (CKA, Procrustes, RV) lose signal after width/depth null-calibration, but local neighbor-identity metrics (mutual-kNN, CKNNA) retain a genuine, calibration-robust convergence signal. PRH survives in a narrower, local/topological form; only the strong global-spectral reading is killed. "ARH disproves PRH" is an overstatement the evidence explicitly warns against. The narrower, correct inference (ARH kills the global-spectral mechanism specifically) does land on OPRD-Bridge: PCA+MSE-in-rank-r-space is precisely a global-spectral/linear-subspace method, the exact family ARH shows is confounded — so OPRD-Bridge's specific mechanism is undermined, even though "PRH" as a whole is not falsified. Additional complications found: mutual-kNN's survival is itself evaluation-scale-fragile (Back into Plato's Cave, 2604.18572), and representational alignment is weakest/causally near-inert exactly in the generation-token region OPRD targets (Convergence Without Understanding, 2605.23315) — undermining hidden-state matching generally, pointwise or relational, beyond just the PRH/ARH framing.</reasoning>
<parameter name="salvage">Weaker, defensible claim: ARH recalibrates rather than disproves PRH — it kills the global-spectral/linear-subspace form of convergence (CKA, Procrustes, PCA-style) while local neighbor-identity convergence survives. Since OPRD-Bridge's PCA+MSE is exactly a global-spectral mechanism, ARH does undermine that specific method's theoretical justification and motivates switching to a local-neighbor-identity loss — but it does not falsify PRH or OPRD-Bridge's premise wholesale, and even the surviving local signal (mutual-kNN) is itself scale-fragile and possibly causally inert in generation-token regions, so switching mechanisms alone doesn't guarantee the fix works.</salvage>

The claim conflates two distinct assertions the evidence carefully separates. (1) Measurement claim: ARH shows global spectral metrics (CKA, Procrustes, RV) lose their scaling signal after width/depth null-calibration, while local neighbor-identity (mKNN/CKNNA) survives — well-supported (digest-arh.md, sweep-prh-arh.md, direct quotes). (2) The claim's leap — "ARH disproves PRH" — is explicitly contradicted by the paper's own framing ("Revisiting," not "Refuting") and 5 independent secondary sources: "refines rather than completely disproves," "PRH survives locally, fails globally." ARH narrows/relocates PRH's convergence claim from global to local structure; it does not falsify PRH. Further, ARH is "purely a measurement/calibration paper" on independently-trained, already-capable models at inference time — no training-objective claims — so "OPRD-Bridge rests on a falsified premise" overstates even the narrower true finding: PCA+MSE is undermined as a measurement-validity analogy, not a demonstrated method failure (sweep-prh-arh.md sec.7: no paper shows PCA-projector bridging actually fail empirically). Compounding threats: mKNN's own "survival" is evaluation-regime-fragile (Back into Plato's Cave, 2604.18572), and alignment is weakest/causally-inert exactly in post-decision/generation tokens where OPRD applies its loss (Convergence Without Understanding, 2605.23315) — threatening any hidden-state loss, pointwise or relational, alike.
votes.salvage: ARH narrows, not disproves, PRH: global-spectral alignment (CKA/Procrustes/RV) loses its scaling signal after confound calibration, while local neighbor-identity alignment survives. This is a legitimate measurement-validity critique specifically of PCA/spectral-style bridges like OPRD-Bridge's PCA+MSE, motivating a switch to a local-neighbor-identity loss as theoretically better-grounded — but it's an analogy from an inference-time measurement result to a training-time prescription, not proof PCA+MSE fails empirically, and the alternative (mKNN loss) has its own unresolved fragility the plan must test, not assume.

ARH keeps a convergence claim, just relocates it from global spectral metrics (CKA, Procrustes, RSA — exactly what dies under null-calibration) to local neighbor-identity (mKNN, CKNNA — which *increases* with scale, 0.10→0.19 calibrated). claim: Relational objectives outperform pointwise MSE for representation distillation, especially cross-architecture.

votes.reasoning: Mixed-to-negative base rate, not a clean win. In the most-cited apples-to-apples benchmark (CRD/RepDistiller, CIFAR-100, 5-seed avg), no-negatives relational losses (RKD, PKT, SP) roughly tie or lose to vanilla pointwise KD; the only relational family that reliably wins (CRD/CoDIR) uses contrastive negatives. VanillaKD (NeurIPS'23) shows much of the "fancy loss beats vanilla" literature is a tuning/scale artifact, and a 2026 hidden-layer-distillation study (2605.11513) finds hidden-state losses' edge over well-tuned pointwise/logit KD is regime-dependent and often vanishes. Cross-architecture specifically: TinyBERT solves width mismatch with plain pointwise MSE + a learned linear map (no relational component), a standard strong baseline neither OPRD-Bridge nor any relational alternative has been shown to beat. Positive evidence exists but is narrower than the claim: MiniLMv2 (self-attention relation transfer dissolves head/width mismatch), MLDR-KD (cross-arch relation-KL, vision), PHF (temporal transition-geometry loss beats pointwise MSE by +1.5-2.2pts on Qwen3 1.7B/4B/8B on-policy self-distillation, same-architecture), and CKA-QAD (global Gram/CKA loss improves reasoning accuracy in RL-post-trained LLMs, also same-architecture). These wins come from specific mechanisms (contrastive negatives, self-attention-specific relations, temporal trajectories, or global spectral matching), not the generic "local-neighbor-identity, no negatives" design ARH motivates -- and no paper tests that exact design against pointwise MSE in a cross-architecture LLM reasoning setting.
votes.salvage: Narrow version survives: specific relational mechanisms (contrastive-with-negatives, self-attention relation transfer, temporal-trajectory geometry, or global CKA/Gram) beat pointwise MSE in documented settings, including some cross-architecture width-mismatch cases (MiniLMv2, MLDR-KD). But generic no-negatives/identity-only relational losses show no reliable base-rate win, and ARH-style local-neighbor-identity loss vs. pointwise MSE for cross-architecture LLM distillation remains an untested comparison, not an established result.

votes.reasoning: The claim, read as a general law ("relational > pointwise, esp. cross-arch"), is contradicted by its own reference class. In CRD/RepDistiller (5-seed CIFAR-100), the no-negatives relational family the plan actually wants (RKD, PKT, SP) roughly ties or *loses* to vanilla pointwise KD (e.g. RKD -1.4 to -1.6pts vs KD on 3/3 pairs); the only relational method that reliably wins (CRD) uses contrastive negatives — a mechanism the target plan explicitly excludes, so the "winning" evidence doesn't transfer to the excluded variant. VanillaKD (NeurIPS'23) independently shows "fancy loss beats vanilla" is often a tuning/scale artifact. For the cross-architecture clause specifically: TinyBERT is a well-established counter-example where plain pointwise MSE + a learned linear map solves width mismatch with no relational component, and no source found runs a controlled head-to-head of relational-vs-pointwise-MSE-with-linear-map in the same cross-arch LLM setting — the pro-relational cross-arch evidence (MiniLMv2, MLDR-KD, PHF, CKA-QAD) is real but comes from different papers/settings/mechanisms (self-attention relations, global Gram/CKA, temporal transition geometry), not a controlled ablation against the pointwise baseline it needs to beat. There's also a metric-vs-training-objective gap: ARH's "local identity survives" is a measurement finding on independently-trained models, never tested as a training loss, so citing it as support for "relational training objectives win" is an unvalidated extrapolation.
votes.salvage: Narrower, defensible claim: specific relational mechanisms that exploit either (a) contrastive negatives (CRD/CoDIR) or (b) architecture-agnostic relation structures (self-attention relation transfer in MiniLMv2, class/sample relation-KL in MLDR-KD, global CKA/Gram in CKA-QAD) can outperform pointwise MSE in some cross-architecture settings — but "relational" as a bare category, especially the no-negatives local-neighbor-identity variant the plan proposes, is not established as superior, and must beat both a well-tuned pointwise-MSE baseline and a pointwise-MSE+learned-linear-map baseline (TinyBERT-style) in a controlled same-setting ablation before the claim holds for OPRD-Bridge/ARH-Bridge.

claim: Contrastive-KD gains reported by CRD/CoDIR are robust and would transfer to on-policy LLM reasoning distillation.

votes.reasoning: CRD (ICLR 2020) is genuinely robust in its own tested domain: RepDistiller's 5-seed CIFAR-100 benchmark shows it is "the only method to always outperform KD" among feature-based approaches. But that's the extent of solid evidence. CoDIR (EMNLP 2020) is BERT/NLU encoder compression, not generative reasoning. Neither paper tests, nor has any found paper tested, contrastive hidden-state KD on on-policy LLM reasoning rollouts — domain gap is total: classification/NLU vs. autoregressive reasoning generation, offline batches vs. on-policy trajectories, small CNN/BERT-base vs. 1.5B+ decoder-only LLMs. Mechanistically, CRD's negatives come from a cross-batch/memory-bank of unrelated samples; there's no established analog for "negative" at the per-token level of a single on-policy trajectory. The closest LLM-reasoning relational win found (PHF, 2606.29340) uses a transition-direction loss with no negatives, not CRD/CoDIR-style contrastive — it doesn't corroborate this specific mechanism. VanillaKD (NeurIPS 2023) shows well-tuned vanilla baselines erode much of the "fancy loss beats vanilla" literature at scale, adding doubt CRD's modest (~1-2pt) small-scale gains would survive scaling even if the mechanism transferred architecturally.
votes.salvage: CRD's within-domain result (vision classification, small CNNs, its own 5-seed CIFAR-100 benchmark) is real and replicated by the original authors; CoDIR's critique of L2/MSE's independence assumption is defensible theory. But "transfers to on-policy LLM reasoning distillation" is untested extrapolation, not a result — the plan's exclusion of contrastive/negatives is defensible on evidentiary-absence grounds, not because negatives are proven weaker there.

votes.reasoning:
Both sub-claims fail. (a) "Robust": CRD's own headline result (RepDistiller, CIFAR-100, 5-seed) is real but VanillaKD (NeurIPS 2023) shows much of the "fancy loss beats vanilla KD" literature is a small-scale/under-tuned-baseline artifact — direct citable doubt on robustness even in-domain. CRD/CoDIR are also in the InfoNCE family, which has documented temperature-sensitivity and collapse pathologies (sweep-soft-knn-losses #6), and CRD's win margin depends on memory-bank/negative-sampling choices not stress-tested here. (b) "Transfer to on-policy LLM reasoning distillation": pure extrapolation, zero supporting evidence. CRD = offline CIFAR-100 CNN classification; CoDIR = offline BERT-scale MLM compression. Neither is generative, on-policy, autoregressive, or reasoning-focused, and both rely on cross-sample negatives (other images/sentences in a batch) — a construct that's structurally undefined in a single-teacher, single-rollout, per-token on-policy setting (what would "negatives" even be — other tokens in the same trajectory? other rollouts?). No file in the evidence base reports a contrastive hidden-state KD result on LLM reasoning rollouts. This is a textbook measurement-domain-to-claim-domain gap: evidence establishes a mechanism class's efficacy on offline vision/NLU classification, the claim asserts it for on-policy generative reasoning distillation.</reasoning>
<parameter name="salvage">Contrastive (negatives-based) hidden-state KD is the most consistently strong non-pointwise family in offline/classification KD benchmarks and is worth citing as the reason plan item (B) excludes negatives — but "transfers to on-policy LLM reasoning" is untested and should be stated as an open question requiring its own ablation, not assumed. CRD's win (ICLR 2020, arXiv 1910.10699) is real but domain-narrow: CIFAR-100 CNN classification, 5-seed avg, modest margins (e.g. 73.33→75.51), teacher-forced offline data, dense in-batch negatives (32-256 images) or a MoCo-style memory bank. CoDIR (EMNLP 2020) is BERT/NLU compression, same offline-negatives structure. Neither has been tested — by any paper found across all sweeps — on autoregressive on-policy rollouts, reasoning LLMs, or last-N-token windows. The mechanism that makes CRD/CoDIR win (negatives) is exactly what OPRD's plan (and the target setting) excludes/lacks: on-policy rollouts give few natural negatives per step, and any cross-rollout memory bank would reintroduce the staleness problem OPD/OPRD is designed to avoid. VanillaKD (NeurIPS 2023, 2305.15781) independently shows "fancy-loss-beats-vanilla" claims are often small-scale/undertuned-baseline artifacts that shrink at scale — directly undercutting "robust." No evidence, positive or negative, exists for the specific transfer target (1.5B math-reasoning, on-policy, hidden-state).
votes.salvage: CRD/CoDIR support a narrower claim: contrastive hidden-state losses reliably beat pointwise MSE/KD *in offline, teacher-forced, dense-batch settings with cheap negatives* (vision classification, BERT NLU). Whether that persists on-policy with sparse per-rollout negatives and staleness constraints is untested and should be run as its own ablation, not assumed inherited — and a well-tuned MSE baseline must be cleared first per VanillaKD.

claim: ARH itself is methodologically sound: only neighbor identity survives null-calibration, and this generalizes beyond the models/tasks ARH tested.

votes.reasoning: Methodological soundness within-scope is plausible (permutation-null width/depth calibration is a genuine, principled fix, consistent with prior CKA-gameability critiques, arXiv 2210.16156/2405.01012) but the generalization half of C4 is directly contradicted, not just unsupported. ARH's own stated limitation says findings "apply to independently sampled image-text pairs but may not generalize," and flags that the exchangeability assumption "fails on sequential/clustered datasets" — exactly the token-sequence regime OPRD needs. Independent empirical work, "Back into Plato's Cave" (2604.18572), directly contradicts the "survives" claim on a different axis: mutual-kNN alignment "degrades substantially" when the eval set scales from ~1K to millions of samples, and newer-model alignment trends don't replicate. ARH's tests were also exclusively on independently-trained, static (non-training-intervention) cross-modal model pairs (n≈1024, 204 pairs) — never on intra-training, token-level, or on-policy generation settings, and "Convergence Without Understanding" (2605.23315) shows representational alignment (of any flavor) behaves qualitatively differently and is causally near-inert in exactly the generation-token regime OPRD/ARH-Bridge would apply it to.
votes.salvage: ARH's calibration procedure is sound and its neighbor-identity-survives finding holds within its tested regime: independently-trained vision/language/video foundation-model pairs, ~1K-sample probe sets, width/depth as the confound axis. It does not establish (and its own limitations section disclaims) generalization to larger eval scales (contradicted by Back into Plato's Cave), non-exchangeable/sequential token data, or training-time/on-policy generation-token settings — exactly where OPRD would need it to hold.

Independent evidence sharpens the refutation: "Back into Plato's Cave" (2604.18572) shows the very metric ARH says survives (mutual-kNN) degrades substantially when eval-set scale grows from ~1K to millions of samples — a fragility axis orthogonal to and untested by ARH's width/depth calibration. claim: Because OPRD-Bridge is motivated by PRH, ARH being right implies PCA+MSE should underperform a neighbor-identity bridge in practice.

votes.reasoning:
Claim C5 makes a category error the ARH paper itself forecloses. digest-arh.md §7 (5 independent sources) states ARH is "purely a measurement/calibration paper" studying independently-trained models at inference time — it "does not discuss alignment as a training objective," and there is "a genuine, un-closed inferential gap" between "this metric survives calibration when measuring naturally-aligned models" and "training to match it beats pointwise MSE." Direct empirical counter-evidence also exists: (1) sweep-relational-kd.md — no-negatives relational losses (RKD/PKT/SP, the exact family of a neighbor-identity bridge) "roughly tie or lose to vanilla pointwise KD" in standard CRD benchmarks; (2) sweep-cross-arch-bridge.md/sweep-update-geometry.md — CKA-QAD, a *global*-spectral (PRH-flavored, PCA-adjacent) loss, already beats output-only matching on reasoning recovery in RL-post-trained LLMs, the opposite direction predicted; (3) sweep-prh-arh.md's "Convergence Without Understanding" shows alignment of any kind is weakest/causally inert exactly on post-decision generation tokens where OPRD operates, threatening both mechanisms equally rather than favoring one; (4) OPRD's own Table 4 shows PCA+MSE bridge already loses to plain OPD top-1, so any competent alternative (not specifically neighbor-identity) could plausibly beat it.</reasoning>

Whether neighbor-identity beats PCA+MSE in practice is an open empirical question that must be run, not inferred from ARH, given relational-KD's mixed base rate and CKA-QAD's counter-example.</salvage>

Claim conflates a measurement claim with a training/mechanism claim. ARH (2602.14486) is explicitly post-hoc statistical calibration of similarity metrics on independently-trained, off-the-shelf models — digest-arh.md §6-7 quotes two independent sources stating the paper "makes no claims about why... or propose training mechanisms" and never tests neighbor-identity as a training loss (sweep-soft-knn-losses.md confirms this too: k fixed at 10, no training use). OPRD-Bridge is an actively-trained, gradient-supervised regime — a different setting ARH's evidence never covers (digest-arh.md explicitly flags this "scope mismatch, not just domain mismatch"). Directional support exists (RSA/Procrustes, the distance-based family closest to PCA, do lose signal under calibration — sweep-prh-arh.md §2,10), so the *motivation* for PCA+MSE is weakened. But "should underperform in practice" requires an empirical training-loss comparison no cited paper runs, and there's live counter-evidence: CKA-QAD (sweep-update-geometry.md, sweep-relational-kd.md) shows a plain global-spectral CKA/Gram training loss *improving* reasoning recovery in RL-post-trained LLMs, and OPRD's own PCA+MSE reportedly reaches ~95% cosine similarity bridge quality — an existence proof it isn't obviously broken. mutual-kNN's own calibrated survival is also evaluation-regime-fragile at scale (Plato's Cave, 2604.18572), so even the "neighbor-identity wins" side isn't secure.
votes.salvage: ARH gives a legitimate theoretical reason to be *suspicious* of PCA+MSE's PRH-based justification and to predict it may underperform a neighbor-identity bridge — worth testing head-to-head. claim: The prefix-heavy position bias found for output-space OPD will transfer to hidden-state (OPRD) supervision.

votes.reasoning: No paper tests OPD-vs-OPRD position bias directly. The position-bias paper (2606.22600) is confirmed pure output-KL/reward-space — zero hidden-state evidence (digest-posbias.md §2). Its own mechanism (Prop. 1) attributes the prefix bias to sampling-variance decay of a single-sample reverse-KL estimator as student rollouts drift off-teacher-support — a mechanism OPRD's Theorem 1 explicitly claims does not apply to its dense, zero-variance pointwise-MSE gradient. More concretely, OPRD's own Fig. 8 diagnostic (digest-oprd.md §3.1) shows the practical opposite pattern used as a design choice: OPRD deliberately targets the response *suffix* (last k=2000 tokens, precisely where teacher-student hidden-state divergence is largest) as its default and reports strong gains there (Table 2) — the exact region OPD's paper found training "barely learns anything." This isn't a controlled ablation isolating suffix-only OPRD, so it's not a clean refutation, but it's a real natural counter-example against naive transfer of "suffix training fails."
